Will the vaults look more beautiful by day or by night? Azul Duel invites you to play with light and pit opposites against each other. This competitive strategic game for two players retains the purity and elegance of the original Azul while adding an extra tactical dimension in which you determine the pattern in which tiles will be placed, in addition to drafting tiles to complete that pattern. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 On Your Turn 3 Placing Tiles, Using Bonuses, End of Round Scoring 4 End Game Scoring Overview Azul duel is a new game based on the Azul theme both designed by Michael Kiesling. The goal is to have the most points at the end of the 5th round. On Your Turn You can either: 1) Select a faceup dome tile. (You must do this twice each round. You can draw tiles from the facedown stack and keep one, but you lose one point for each facedown tile you draw). 2) Select all the tiles of one colour from the Sun side of a tile, select what order to place the remaining tiles on to the moon space. 3) Select 1 tile colour from the top of a moon space, and take all tiles of that colour from all moons, top tile only. 4) Take a revealed bonus chip. If you take from the large factory moon side with the 1 player marker you will become the first player and lose 2 points. Once the moon area is empty the bonus chip is available for selection. Placing Tiles, Using Bonuses, End of Round Scoring When you gain tiles all of them must go in a single pattern line, any leftovers are broken and cause you negative points based on 1-4 tiles, any over 4 are ignored. At the end of the round full pattern lines will trigger, you will move 1 tile to an open space on a dome tile, scoring 1 point if it is adjacent to nothing, if it has tiles adjacent in a row or column score 1 point for each tile scoring the new tile multiple times once for the column and once for the row. Any tiles that do not have home from a full pattern line will stay, but can be moved later if a dome plate comes up. If you can never move your tiles they will break losing you points. You can use bonus chips to help fill your pattern lines. Select chips matching your missing tile colour, or any 3 chips then move the chip to a dome tile. If you have a special dome tile, and have filled it in, you fill the tile with a special tile, and score the points on the far right of that row, then also count that special tile in the future for row and column scoring. End Game Scoring By this time your player board will be full of dome tiles so you will no longer take dome tiles. Score the 3 scoring tiles at the end of the game, hover over the tile to see its scoring condition during the game. The beginner game mode will always have these 3 end game scoring conditions: 1) 3 points for each completed row 2) 7 points for each completed column 3) 10 points for each completed 6 tile diagonal line. Ties are broken by the player holding the 1st player token. [Rating: 1/10] Getting real tired of this fad. Who is making all these publishers shove out these duel games? This is unnecessary. Azul did not need a duel version and this is not worthy of being published.  Cash grab. Played on BGA.

[Rating: 1/10] But, one must ask—why? Regular AZUL is one of the rare games that plays well with all player counts, including 2-player, which turns it into a game of direct conflict and defensive posturing. Nothing needed to be "fixed". What we have here is a sad victim of bloat. Convoluted mechanisms and rules that complicate the game without adding anything substantially meaningful beyond what AZUL already offers. The entire dome plate system is silly, fruitless, cumbersome. Bonus tiles...again, why? The sun/moon delineations of the tile are a monumental hassle, sitting there attempting to re-order the rem

[Rating: 1/10] Ugh..Azul is a great 2p game, this is worse in every way. Convoluted mechanisms that complicate the game adding nothing meaningful besides making the game more opaque, longer and heads down.  Avoid.

[Rating: 3/10] Played it twice and sold it. Has even less theme than the original Azul. Designer threw the kitchen sink at the game, with a ton of pointless and nonsensical rules. I am not a fan of the original Azul, but I would much rather play that at two players, than this game.

[Rating: 3/10] As someone that has played first Azul mostly 2p (+2000 games), this is not any better version. It gives you a lot of freedom and it's colorful, that's all. You like colors and customizing your board? this is probably a nice option for you but it's overcomplicated and give you unnecessary options that doesn't make it more fun. In first azul you end the game because one of the players has completed a row. In this version you play 5 rounds, that's all. You mix colors, don't necessarily follow a color pattern,... it doesn't feel like a well thought game... Actually it's a terrible game.

[Rating: 3/10] Wow.... it's terrible. Getting through five rounds of this was a chore. Considering that the original game is a great 2p game, this is incredibly unnecessary.

[Rating: 3/10] The original didn't need a 2p only version. I didn't care for the larger board, limitations on the number of tiles you get per round, and the limited number of rounds. Rated a 3, not due to it being "bad", as I think some people will enjoy it. I rated it a 3 due to the description "won't play this again".

[Rating: 3/10] If you love Azul, don't buy this variant. My wife and I love the Azul series, with every game rated a 8+, but this one will be never played again.  The game-play isn't satisfying. No interaction, while duel is in the name ...

[Rating: 3/10] Significantly more complicated version of the other Azul games, all of which play great at 2 players. Literally no need or desire to play this again.

[Rating: 3/10] BGA only. This actually feels unnecessary. It is longer, slower, and somehow more boring than the original. I had hopes for it, but alas, it misses the mark. OG Azul has a perfectly fine 2p experience. This offering is just bad, lacks any kind of interesting gameplay, and I just can't get onboard with it at all.

[Rating: 3/10] Played twice on BGA and that was enough for me I'll never try it again. I like my Azul with more guardrails and simpler. I'm not putting energy or effort in this overly abstract version - I'll still with standard or stained glass.
